sec: History, CDC staging and AIDS-defining malignancies, viral and fungal illnesses

items.q: In which year is the first reported case of HIV printed?
What is printed about the origin of the first reported case?
opts: It was reported from an African patient
It was reported from an American infant
It was reported from a European blood donor
It was reported from an Asian traveller

items.q: Which old name for the virus is printed on this page?
CDC staging — match the stage to the CD4 count — 1) Stage 1 2) Stage 2 3) Stage 3 … A) 200-499 cells/mm³ B) below 200 cells/mm³ C) 500 or more cells/mm³
Which CD4 percentage is printed for stage 2 disease?
items.exp: Stage 2 prints a CD4 percentage of 14-28. (Book p1061)

items.q: Which CD4 percentage is printed for stage 3 disease?
items.exp: Stage 3 prints a CD4 percentage below 14. (Book p1061)

items.q: CDC stages — match the stage to its clinical evidence — 1) Stage 0 2) Stage 1 and 2 3) Stage 3 … A) No AIDS-defining condition B) Documentation of AIDS-defining conditions C) Early HIV infection
items.exp: 'Stage 0 : Early HIV infection'; stages 1 and 2 print 'No AIDS-defining condition'; stage 3 prints 'Documentation of AIDS-defining conditions'. (Book p1061)

items.q: AIDS-defining malignancies — match — 1) Lymphomas 2) Others … A) Invasive cervical cancer and Kaposi's sarcoma B) Burkitt's lymphoma, immunoblastic lymphoma (EBV mediated), primary CNS lymphoma
items.exp: '1. malignancies : · Lymphomas : Burkitt's lymphoma, Immunoblastic lymphoma (EBV mediated), Primary CNS lymphoma; · Invasive cervical cancer; · Kaposi's sarcoma'. (Book p1061)

items.q: How is the EBV relationship printed among the AIDS-defining lymphomas?
opts: Primary CNS lymphoma is EBV mediated
No lymphoma is linked to EBV

items.q: AIDS-defining viral infections — match the virus to the lesion — 1) CMV 2) HSV 3) JC virus … A) Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy B) Disease other than liver, spleen and lymph node involvement C) Disease other than zoster
items.exp: '2. Viral infections : · Cytomegalovirus (other than liver, spleen and lymph node involvement); · Herpes simplex (except zoster); JC virus : Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy'. (Book p1061)

items.q: Which JC-virus disease is listed as AIDS defining?
AIDS-defining fungal infections — match — 1) Candidiasis 2) Cryptococcosis 3) Pneumocystis … A) Extrapulmonary disease B) Pneumocystis jirovecii C) Bronchi, trachea, lungs or oesophagus
items.exp: '3. Fungal infections : · Candidiasis of bronchi/trachea/lungs/oesophagus; · Cryptococcosis (extrapulmonary); Pneumocystis jirovecii'. (Book p1061)

items.q: Which is NOT printed among the AIDS-defining infections on this page?
opts: Cytomegalovirus disease outside liver, spleen and nodes
items.exp: Oral hairy leukoplakia is a category B condition; the AIDS-defining list has CMV, HSV, JC virus, candidiasis of bronchi/trachea/lungs/oesophagus, cryptococcosis and Pneumocystis. (Book p1061)

items.q: A patient with HIV has a CD4 count of 150 cells/mm³ and oesophageal candidiasis. Which CDC stage and category does the page support?
opts: Stage 3 (below 200 cells/mm³) with an AIDS-defining condition
Stage 1, because candidiasis is not AIDS defining
Stage 2, because the count is above 100
items.exp: CD4 below 200 with documentation of an AIDS-defining condition is stage 3; oesophageal candidiasis is on the AIDS-defining fungal list. (Book p1061)
